title: Evidence-based answer
summary: Require support for each substantive claim rather than a list of impressive links.

sections.label: Claim record
items: Atomic claim and its status: observed, inferred, proposed, or unresolved.
Exact source identifier, passage/section, and version.
Scope that affects the claim. This might be a software version and environment, or a jurisdiction, population and effective period for a domain assertion.

sections.label: Verification layers
sections.text: A working link proves availability, not support. A relevant passage may still fail to support the claim. A supported claim may still be inapplicable to the requested scope.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: The reader can reproduce the evidential basis. Missing support leads to a useful uncertainty statement rather than a fabricated answer.

catalog.applicability: Use this when an answer or finding must carry support for each substantive claim, with its status, exact source, scope and uncertainty. A working link, a relevant passage and a supported claim are different layers, and missing support should produce an uncertainty statement rather than a fabricated answer.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
